business_summary: SoFi Technologies is classed as fintech and banking. Revenue has compounded about 18% a year over three years and about 43% over five. Net profit is positive: 481.32 USD m in FY25 and 636.26 USD m over the last four quarters. Several bank-inapplicable ratios are not available.
why_own: The case rests on sustained revenue growth (about 18% a year over three years) together with profits that have turned positive, with no loss-making quarter in the last four. Evidence is thin: there are no supplied documents, profit growth is undefined, and there is no P/E history to compare against, so the thesis is limited to a few metric drivers.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate; the 3-year revenue CAGR is 17.99% today. (warn line tightened by code from 12 to 12.59.)
Profitability on equity improves from its current low level; FY25 ROE is 5.66%, so the profits must earn a better return on equity as the business grows.
The company stays profitable every quarter; none of the last 4 quarters was loss-making.

kill_criteria.description: More than 2 of the last 4 quarters are loss-making, which would undo the profitability case.
ROE falls below 2%, meaning profits no longer earn a meaningful return on equity.

risks.statement: Valuation is demanding relative to returns: P/E is 29.8x and price/book is 1.81x while ROE is only 5.66%. Whether this is high against its own history is untested, because P/E history is unavailable.
The profit record is short. Net profit growth over 3 years is undefined because profit was zero or negative at the start or end of the period, so the durability of current profits is unproven.
Revenue growth has slowed from the 5-year pace (43.07% CAGR) to the 3-year pace (17.99% CAGR). The evidence does not say why, so further slowing is a risk.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if SoFi's profits are a short, cyclical upswing rather than durable earnings. At 29.8x earnings and 1.81x book, the price assumes ROE climbs well above 5.66%. The tripwires are too lenient to flag that. ROE only breaks below 2%, and the kill rule needs 3 of 4 quarters to be loss-making. Revenue growth has already slowed from 43% to 18% a year, and the break line of 8% allows more than a halving. With no profit-growth history and no P/E history, the 'INTACT' status rests on three backward-looking metrics. What would change this view: Several more quarters of profit at or above the current trailing level, with ROE rising clearly above the 5.66% FY25 level and revenue growth holding near the 18% 3-year pace, would drop the objection.
